focus: Explain step by step what the training actually taught students to do.

output.title: What the Time Management Training Taught Students

scenes.narration: In this video, we unpack the 4 h training: not whether time management sounds useful, but exactly what students were taught to do.
scenes.layout_description: A single student sits beside a large simple clock and open notebook, with an orange arrow pointing into the notebook.
scenes.visual_prompt: Solid cream background, hand-drawn black ink student, clock, and notebook; orange arrow leads from clock to notebook, with yellow highlights on the notebook.

scenes.narration: The study asked whether teaching specific time management strategies could increase perceived control of time and reduce perceived stress, measured with tension.
scenes.layout_description: A balance scale shows a clock on one side and a tense face on the other, with an upward arrow near the clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink balance scale on cream background; clock icon highlighted yellow, tense face circled orange, simple handwritten labels.

scenes.narration: Undergraduate students at a medium-sized German university joined voluntarily as an extracurricular activity, with no incentives, and trained in groups of about ten students.
scenes.layout_description: A small group of students gathers around a table, with a simple university building in the background.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink group of about ten simplified students around a table; orange circle around the group, yellow windows on small university building.

scenes.narration: All participants completed questionnaires directly before training; the main analyses used the 23 students who answered again 2 and 4 weeks afterward.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline runs left to right with three clipboard icons and a small group marked 23 at the end.
scenes.visual_prompt: Cream background with black ink timeline, three simple clipboards, orange dots at before, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks, yellow highlight behind 23.

scenes.narration: The training was organized around prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring, all drawn from Häfner and Stock’s earlier program.
scenes.layout_description: Five simple stepping stones cross the slide from left to right, each holding a small icon for one training part.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink stepping stones on cream background; icons include star, flag, path, calendar, check mark; orange arrows connect stones with yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: First, students reflected on their current activities, including academic tasks and extracurricular activities, and wrote these different activities down for later review.
scenes.layout_description: A student writes a long list, with book and activity icons floating nearby.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn student at desk with notebook list; black ink book, bag, and simple hobby icons; orange pen and yellow list lines.

scenes.narration: Then they considered how important each activity was for their study goals, trying to identify the most important ones among all listed.
scenes.layout_description: A list is shown with several items, and three are circled with orange as most important.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink paper list on cream background; orange circles mark selected lines, yellow star beside the top chosen item, simple graduation cap icon.

scenes.narration: This self-reflection used questions like, which activities are most important, and why are these activities important to me for my studies right now?
scenes.layout_description: A student looks at two large question marks above a notebook of activities.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink student with thoughtful expression; notebook open, orange question marks overhead, yellow glow around one selected line.

scenes.narration: After clarifying important activities, students defined concrete, challenging, and proximal goals for them, moving from vague intentions toward specified study goals instead.
scenes.layout_description: A foggy-looking scribble on the left changes into a clear flag on the right along an orange arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink scribble cloud labeled as vague, orange arrow to a neat flag on a hill; yellow highlight around flag, cream background.

scenes.narration: They asked what they wanted to achieve in detail and defined deadlines, so each important activity had a clearer target to pursue.
scenes.layout_description: A target with a flag sits beside a calendar page, connected to a student’s checklist.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink calendar, target, and checklist; orange bullseye ring, yellow deadline square on calendar, plenty of white space.

scenes.narration: Next came strategy development: students wrote down different steps toward their goals, set priorities for these steps, and planned how to start.
scenes.layout_description: A staircase leads from a student to a flag, with numbered steps and an orange arrow upward.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink student at bottom of simple staircase; steps highlighted yellow, orange arrow climbs toward flag, handwritten short labels.

scenes.narration: In the same phase, they thought about possible obstacles and what to do to overcome them, before problems appeared in their plans.
scenes.layout_description: A planned path bends around a small barrier, with an orange detour arrow showing another route.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink path with a rock barrier; orange curved arrow around obstacle, yellow highlight on the alternate route, cream background.

scenes.narration: The training also emphasized proximal deadlines for steps to goal achievement, not only broad goals somewhere in the future for students' work.
scenes.layout_description: A far flag is broken into several nearer flags along a path, each beside a small calendar square.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink path with multiple small flags before a distant flag; orange circles around near flags, yellow calendar squares, clean cream background.

scenes.narration: The fourth part focused on daily planning, where trainees decided what they wanted to do and when during their study work periods.
scenes.layout_description: A large daily planner page fills the center, with time blocks and a student pointing to one block.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink planner page with simple blocks; orange marker points to a chosen block, yellow highlights show planned study times.

scenes.narration: They developed a concrete schedule for their studies, asking which important tasks should receive attention tomorrow and where work would happen then.
scenes.layout_description: A tomorrow page shows one highlighted task and a simple desk icon as the planned place.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink calendar page labeled tomorrow, desk icon, and task line; yellow highlight on task, orange arrow from task to desk.

scenes.narration: Daily planning included questions about when and where to complete tasks, and how much time should be scheduled for different tasks overall.
scenes.layout_description: Three small panels show a clock, a desk, and a shaded time block.
scenes.visual_prompt: Cream background with three black ink icons in a row: clock, desk, calendar block; orange arrows connect them, yellow shading on time block.

scenes.narration: Students also considered how they could avoid distractions, keeping the plan connected to focused action rather than merely listing tasks on paper.
scenes.layout_description: A student studies at a desk while distracting symbols are gently pushed aside by an orange arrow.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink student working; small distraction icons off to the side, orange arrow moving them away, yellow focus circle around notebook.

scenes.narration: The last part taught monitoring of task completion: students were instructed to check each day which tasks they had completed so far.
scenes.layout_description: A daily checklist appears with several check marks, held by a student at the end of a day.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink checklist with check marks; student holding it beside a small setting sun icon, orange check marks and yellow highlight on completed lines.

scenes.narration: Monitoring also meant seeing what still had to be done, making progress and remaining tasks visible at the end of each day.
scenes.layout_description: Two columns on a page show completed tasks and remaining tasks, with an orange line dividing them.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink notebook page with two columns; left has check marks, right has open circles, orange divider, yellow highlight on progress.

scenes.narration: The authors connected these strategies to student demands named in prior research: self-organized learning, time pressures, and high workload among students in studies.
scenes.layout_description: A student carries books, a clock, and a loose study plan, while the training steps appear as tools nearby.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink student with stack of books and clock; orange tool icons for plan and checklist, yellow highlights on the helpful tools.

scenes.narration: To check transfer, the study measured time management behaviour with 18 items covering behaviours such as prioritizing, setting clear goals, and monitoring.
scenes.layout_description: A questionnaire page sits beside icons for a star, flag, and checklist.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink survey sheet with small boxes; orange circles around star, flag, checklist icons, yellow highlight behind 18 items.

scenes.narration: Reported use of the taught strategies showed a nearly significant increase after 2 weeks and a significant increase after 4 weeks afterward.
scenes.layout_description: A simple upward line passes through two time points, with the later point brighter than the earlier one.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line graph without extra numbers; orange line rises from before to 2 weeks to 4 weeks, yellow glow on 4 weeks point.

scenes.narration: For outcomes, trainees reported significantly less perceived stress, measured with tension, 2 and 4 weeks after training than before the training began.
scenes.layout_description: A tense face beside a clock becomes calmer across a three-point timeline.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink faces along a timeline; first tense, later calmer; orange arrows between them, yellow highlights under 2 and 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: Perceived control of time showed only a tendency in the expected direction at 2 weeks, then a significant increase at 4 weeks.
scenes.layout_description: A student gradually steadies a large clock, with the strongest highlight at the final time point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink student holding clock at three stages; orange arrows show movement, yellow highlight strongest around final steady clock.

scenes.narration: Demands, the control variable for perceived, self-reported demands, did not show significant changes 2 weeks or 4 weeks after training ended either.
scenes.layout_description: A level horizontal line runs across three time points above a pile of tasks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink pile of papers under a flat line; orange dots at before, 2 weeks, 4 weeks; yellow equal sign near line.

scenes.narration: The authors noted stronger effects for students with no or little prior time-management experience than for those with moderate or some experience.
scenes.layout_description: Two students stand beside different-sized upward arrows, with the larger arrow beside the student holding an empty toolbox.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink two simplified students; one with empty toolbox and larger orange arrow, other with partly filled toolbox and smaller arrow, yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: Their practical takeaway was cautious: these strategies might be good advice, but more studies are needed before robust practical implications can follow.
scenes.layout_description: A path of the five training steps continues toward a question mark and a small research notebook.
scenes.visual_prompt: Cream background with black ink stepping stones, flag, checklist, and research notebook; orange path arrow continues forward, yellow question mark at the end.
